root_motivation: Bootstrap autobuilder under its own discipline. The companion Rust binary owns the load-bearing parts of the Stage 1–5 pipeline (intake, scaffold, loop, gate, postmortem, evolve). The first artifact whose existence the gate can verify on itself is the 7-receipt risk-gate machinery — proving the binary can produce and walk all seven receipts on its own repo is the v1 acceptance test for the gate model itself.
user_persona: The autobuilder skill orchestrator (a Claude session) and the human invoking `/autobuilder` from their own project. Both shell out to this binary for the receipt + gate steps that must not live in bash.

acceptance_criteria.description: `autobuilder rollback-plan --project <dir> --base <ref>` dry-runs git revert via merge-tree, writes target/autobuilder/rollback.md, and emits a digest-bound receipts/rollback-plan.json with verdict pass|block.
acceptance_criteria.test: scripts/run-metrics.sh — smoke against the autobuilder repo itself

acceptance_criteria.description: `autobuilder vti-plan --project <dir> --base <ref>` reads agent/proof-lanes.toml, routes every changed file from <base>..HEAD to ≥1 lane (confidence ≥ 0.70), and emits a digest-bound receipts/vti-plan.json.
acceptance_criteria.test: scripts/run-metrics.sh — smoke against the autobuilder repo itself

acceptance_criteria.description: `autobuilder reviewer-agent prepare` assembles a review-request packet (HEAD, base, intent_card_sha256, commits, changed_files); `autobuilder reviewer-agent finalize --input <decision.json>` validates the subagent's JSON against the schema in prompts/reviewer-agent.md and emits a digest-bound receipts/reviewer-agent.json.
acceptance_criteria.test: scripts/run-metrics.sh — smoke against the autobuilder repo itself

acceptance_criteria.description: `autobuilder ci-checks --project <dir>` shells out to `gh run list --commit <head>` and refuses to emit verdict=pass without at least one workflow run with conclusion=success on HEAD.
acceptance_criteria.test: scripts/run-metrics.sh — smoke against the autobuilder repo itself

acceptance_criteria.description: `autobuilder gate --project <dir>` walks target/autobuilder/receipts/{intake,vti-plan,proof-receipt,risk-gate,reviewer-agent,rollback-plan,ci-checks}.json, verifies schema + head_sha + verdict on each, and emits target/autobuilder/release-receipt.json with the aggregated verdict.
acceptance_criteria.test: scripts/run-metrics.sh — smoke against the autobuilder repo itself

acceptance_criteria.description: Strict clippy (clippy::pedantic + workspace lints) passes with -D warnings on the autobuilder bin. Workspace cargo check + cargo test --workspace pass under CI's RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings env.

Every receipt produced by autobuilder includes a sha256 `receipt_digest` over its own canonicalized JSON (keys sorted), plus a UTC `captured_at` (RFC3339). The digest field is overwritten with an empty string before computing the digest so the field is self-binding.
acceptance_criteria.test: src/receipt.rs::write covers every receipt; visual inspection of any emitted receipt JSON

scope: Stage 4 risk gate (7 receipts + release receipt)
non_goals: Spawning Claude subagents from the binary itself (that is the orchestrator's job)
Web-service, WASM, or embedded scaffolding (v1 supports cli + lib only)
Auto-applying self-evolution proposals (always gated for user review)
Re-running the underlying audit/test commands inside `gate` (gate only attests; producers own the work)

five_whys_trace.q: Why a Rust companion binary instead of a pure-skill scaffold?
five_whys_trace.a: Shell is too easy to subvert (set -e off, grep eaten, jq missing). The load-bearing parts — metric extraction, digest binding, schema validation — need a typed implementation under tests.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a 7-receipt gate instead of `cargo test && cargo clippy`?
five_whys_trace.a: Each receipt covers a class of failure that the others miss: clippy doesn't see CI status, tests don't see proof-lane routing, and none of them produce an independent-review record. The gate is what makes 'ready' falsifiable.

five_whys_trace.q: Why bootstrap autobuilder against itself before running it on other projects?
five_whys_trace.a: If the gate model can't certify the binary that produces gate receipts, it can't be trusted on any other project. The meta-bootstrap is the cheapest adversarial test of the whole pipeline.

five_whys_trace.q: Why deny unwrap/expect everywhere in src/ when most of this is glue code?
five_whys_trace.a: Glue code that panics on a missing receipt or malformed JSON destroys the audit trail at exactly the moments the gate matters most. Erroring back to the caller keeps the diagnostic surface alive.

five_whys_trace.q: Why digest-bind every receipt instead of trusting file timestamps?
five_whys_trace.a: Timestamps lie under git checkout. A self-binding sha256 lets the gate detect tampering and lets reviewers re-verify by recomputing on the receipt's own contents.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Where does the autobuilder repo's 'project' live for the gate — repo root or autobuilder/ workspace?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Repo root. agent/, scripts/, target/autobuilder/ all sit at /home/jsy/projects/autobuilder/. Proof-lanes globs use autobuilder/src/** prefix to match `git diff` output.
